title: It’s Time I Let Go Of My Favorite Alien Isolation 2 Theory
description: Alien Isolation 2 stars a new protagonist named Blake. Creative Assembly has been clear about this all summer, but it's only now that I'm letting it sink in. Since I first played a demo of the survival-horror game at Summer Game Fest's Play Days this past June, I've been holding onto a theory that Blake's role in the story is a bait-and-switch--that in short order Blake would be impaled by the Xenomorph and Amanda Ripley, star of the first game, would show up as the real playable character. But it's time I let go of that pet theory of mine. Every time Creative Assembly talks about this game, the team highlights Blake's story. There's too much investment on the team's end for me to keep believing they have a trick up their sleeve. "What I can say is the story focuses on Blake," principal environment artist Archie Whitehead told GameSpot's Miri Teixeira on the Gamescom showfloor following a hands-on demo. "She's been sent to the colony. If you watch the trailer, you see this, like she's been sent there kind of as penance, like she's made a mistake." It's just the latest in a series of confirmations that my theory about Ripley is all wrong. I can see that now. The team told me something similar during Summer Game Fest, but I guess I was too worried about letting them pull a fast one on me to see it. I wanted to spot the twist before it was on-screen. For what it's worth, I had this same theory about Red Dead Redemption 2's Arthur Morgan back in 2018, and that wasn't exactly true--though I guess it was eventually sort of true. It's not that I'd necessarily enjoy Alien Isolation 2 more if Amanda Ripley were the playable character again. It's not that I think this makes the game better in some obvious way. I could see this sequel being memorable with or without her in the driver's seat like that, so I've always been on board for Blake as the protagonist if it shook out that way; I just doubted she actually would be. But today, after hearing it for the third or fourth…

title: Turn-Based-Tactics Fans Are Suddenly Eating Very Well
description: The XCOM series has been effectively on hiatus for many years now, and AAA turn-based-tactics games have been pretty hard to come by recently. That's changing, however, starting with this week's launch of Star Wars Zero Company. It's effectively a marriage of classic XCOM gameplay and Clone Wars-era Star Wars storytelling, and within a few minutes of starting it, I got that same rush of excitement I got the first time I played an XCOM game. Typically, I try to savor turn-based tactical experiences like this as much as possible, because I know it's going to be at least a few years before something like it comes along again. The last XCOM-esque turn-based-tactics game I can even recall playing was Classified: France '44, which released well over two years ago. I enjoyed that one so much that I considered just starting it over again, because there wasn't really anything else like it releasing at the time. But no longer! As part of Gamescom Opening Night Live, Ubisoft revealed Rainbow 6 Tactics. Ditching the first-person-shooter gameplay the series is famous for, Rainbow 6 Tactics is a single-player tactical experience that plays out like a turn-based version of Rainbow Six Siege. You scout enemy positions using drones and then launch your attack, breaching walls and taking down enemies with precision and force. It makes use of the destructible environments Rainbow Six Siege is famous for, but it's all wrapped up in a completely different genre. And just like Zero Company, Rainbow 6 Tactics will be available on Xbox and PS5 in addition to PC, giving it a wide audience when it arrives in 2027. And if you don't have an Xbox, a PS5, or PC, you're still not being left out of the fun as of late. Sure, it's also an RPG, but Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is certainly going to scratch that turn-based-strategy itch. Developer Intelligent Systems is arguably the king of the genre, and based on our hands-on preview of the game, it looks to be absolutely packed with content. There…

title: GTA 6’s Long Wait Has People Realizing Their Own Mortality
description: You might expect people to talk about the visuals, lighting, action sequences, or gunplay after Grand Theft Auto VI's brand-new extended-look trailer showed off over 25 minutes of new footage. But the top comments on Rockstar's YouTube upload of the video deal more with the human condition than expected. In fact, there's quite a bit of talk about death and remembrance. The top comment (at the time of publication) states: "a moment of silence for people that didn't make it here." Meanwhile, another person writes: "Objective: Stay alive till release day." It's been a long wait for GTA 6, especially since GTA 5 originally launched almost 13 years ago. Not only has a lot happened to the gaming industry as a whole since GTA 5 came out, but also to people's personal lives. For instance, another person typed: "Bro, I went through middle school, high school, and college... now I need to request time off work for this." Tragedy has apparently struck others, but not dampered their spirits, as seen in this comment: "I was in a traffic accident in February and lost a leg, but I've still got my two damn hands and my eyes, baby!" There is a lot to take in from the new GTA 6 trailer, such as NPCs noticing if you're openly carrying a weapon in the game. In addition, stealing a car might be a little more complicated this time around. For older vehicles, you can still smash the glass, but newer models apparently require a key cloner. GTA 6 is set to finally release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It sounds like a playthrough of the open-world game could be roughly 80 hours, so plan accordingly this holiday season.

title: GTA 6 Lets You Throw Dog Poop At People
description: A very important piece of news has come to light about GTA 6: You can pick up dog poop and throw it at people in the upcoming open-world crime game. YouTuber TGG visited Rockstar North's offices and spoke with the team, and one of the things he learned was how dog poop can be a weapon. "If someone is out on the street and they're walking their dog, and the dog takes a dump, you can wait for the person to pick up the dog sh** with a doggie bag, and then you can hit that person, making them drop that doggie bag full of dog crap, and then you can actually pick that up and throw it at people," he said. Throwing dog poop at people is not a nice thing to do, and presumably GTA 6's new Red Dead Redemption 2-like honor system will knock you for this, or at least we hope it would. GTA 6 also lets you pet dogs or scold them, and we're hoping anyone who scolds a very good boy also gets a ding to their honor. One of the dogs in GTA 6. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it's coming to market with an enormous amount of hype behind it. GTA 6 is expected to sell many millions of copies--so many that preorders alone could pay for the game's entire development budget.

title: "Hopefully a meteor will strike the earth soon": Game devs talk genAI witchhunts and the importance of honing your visual literacy
description: The era of generative AI has kindled an era of generative AI witchhunts. It's routine right now for videogame developers to fend off accusations of using the technology, even when they are full-throated in their disapproval of ChatGPT, Claude and their ilk. Recent examples include Sandustry, the 2D factory builder from Hooded Horse with strangely haunting physics, and the just-announced Humankind 2, whose creators Amplitude have rushed to assure players that their announcement trailer is genuine live action film. The conversation reflects a shifting idea of what AI-generated imagery 'looks like' - shifting because, strictly speaking, AI-generated imagery has no fixed style or quality. It's derived from whatever data the model is 'fed'. The confusion is exacerbated by the fact that the technology is changing, with new or updated buzzwordy tools being added to the pile. Established hallmarks of generated imagery go out of date fast. Meanwhile, generative AI's advocates muddy the waters, conflating tools and framing their capabilities in ludicrously open-ended, investor-baiting terms. Still, some responsibility falls on regular users who've become accustomed to chucking around claims of "AI slop". Read more

title: GTA 6: All The Biggest Takeaways From The Big New Trailer That You Need To Know
description: Rockstar finally lifted the veil on GTA 6 during a high-profile Netflix event on August 27. The nearly 30-minute video revealed a lot. We saw main characters Jason and Lucia in action in snippets of multiple different missions, while there were cutscenes and character interactions on display as well. The broadcast also featured a new look at some of the updated gameplay systems, like how NPCs will notice if you're carrying a weapon in public, how stealing cars works, and that the game has a Red Dead Redemption 2-style honor system. There were numerous other details big and small to be gleaned from the reveal, along with interviews from developers at Rockstar North. Check out GameSpot's video below in which Jake Dekker runs through 29 different things we noticed in GTA 6 from the big new trailer, and I'm guessing we found some stuff you didn't notice right away. Check out the video below to see it all. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. There is likely going to be a PC edition of the game, but no one should expect it at launch. While Rockstar Games has shown off GTA 6's single-player, the developer has yet to utter a word about anything regarding an online multiplayer mode. GTA 5's GTA Online has been, and continues to be, a huge success for Rockstar, so it only stands to reason that Rockstar would lean into multiplayer for GTA 6 as well.

title: Fable’s Loot Is Meant To Be Meaningful, So Don’t Expect A Bunch Of Minor Upgrades
description: At the heart of many great action-RPGs is a satisfying grind for better loot. Whether it's random chests or quest rewards, it's important to feel like you're getting appropriate payoffs for overcoming challenges. Playground Games, the studio behind the upcoming Fable reboot, told GameSpot it's aiming to make sure that its loot and equipment feels meaningful, with big swings in power level. Creative directors Will Kennedy and Craig Littler told us in an interview at Gamescom that there's lots of variety in the kinds of loot you'll find, and the particularly impactful ones will be new gear. "We want our upgrades to be what we call meaningfully meaningful," Kennedy said. "So you don't get things like, 'Oh, 1% damage,' and things like that. What you get is bigger swings. A good example is the weapon spell we showed. When you first get the weapon spell, you can do a suspend part up in the air. But one of the upgrades you experience is the slam, which really expands the utility and impact of the spell. There's lots of examples like that." With so many options in combat, it's also important to be able to manage your loadouts easily. Kennedy noted that your loadout consists of your melee weapon, ranged weapon, spells, and abilities. Spells and abilities can be upgraded with a skill tree, and then weapons will have their own upgrade path as well. Littler added that the items you find in chests will also play into the game's various systems, including baubles you can give to help your social standing. "You do also find other things in chests," he said. "You might find a gift, for example, that would work with the life system. I don't know what kind of gifts you would find in an old mine, probably a Bag of Blistering or something, but once you've collected that, you can then use that on the NPCs around the world." GameSpot got hands-on with Fable at Gamescom and came away impressed with its combat across two pre-built loadouts, with a hammer, alongside different types of bows…

title: Alien Deathstorm Is A Fun Shooter That (So Far) Needs More Deathstorm
description: Alien Deathstorm is a brand-new action-horror-shooter game from Rebellion. Following the gameplay trailer's reveal at Gamescom, GameSpot was able to go hands-on, and it definitely has a retro feel with interesting-looking mechanics tied to the titular deathstorm that I wish we saw more of in the demo. Alien Deathstorm puts players in the boots of a combat engineer, who becomes stranded on an devastated off-world colony. The planet is being ravaged by a cataclysmic "deathstorm," and it's also overrun by very aggressive aliens. In my interview with producer Martin Bellingham, the developer said it was keeping the location of the colony's planet a secret for now, but I at least recognized the area I explored to be a dilapidated nuclear reactor site. This specific mission required me to survive the stormy conditions and relentless waves of aliens as I fought my way inside the location's reactor core. Navigating to the objective was difficult, as I was often swarmed by waves of the colony's alien threat. The aliens are attracted to sound and any perceived disturbance to the space immediately around them, attacking on sight. Bellingham explained that Alien Deathstorm isn't a stealth game, so these combat encounters will always occur--there's no way to avoid them entirely. However, you still have a choice in how you explore an area and how much noise you're willing to make, allowing you to draw the aliens to you instead of being ambushed by them. You can even use sound to draw the enemies out of their hiding spots or toward areas that are more advantageous for you if you're feeling strategic. There are a few varieties of aliens on this planet, but most notable are the giant retro-styled creatures called soldiers, who look like a mash-up between the Predator and the Alien franchise's famous xenomorphs. The soldier aliens aren't especially difficult to kill; instead, the biggest issue was running out of ammo and trying to scavenge more while they remained hot on my heels.…

title: Saber Boss Reacts To The Death Of Physical Games And Rising Console Prices
description: 2026 has been full of big storylines in gaming, including Sony's announcement that it will end support for physical PlayStation game discs in 2028 and the trend of consoles getting increasingly expensive. Tim Willits, the chief creative officer at Saber Interactive, caught up with GameSpot at Gamescom this week to discuss these topics and offer up a bizarre-sounding possibility for an "AI box" for games. He said he was "surprised how upset people were" about Sony ending support for physical game discs. Willits said he hasn't bought a physical game "in a long time" because he enjoys the convenience of digital games. Willits is not alone, as the share of digital game sales is growing at numerous companies. At the same time, Sony continues to sell millions of physical game discs annually. Willits said Saber still makes "a lot of money" from physical games, especially in Europe, but the trends are different in North America, he observed. Willits went on to say he had an interaction with someone recently who asked him to sign a copy of Doom 3, a game he worked on when he was with id Software. "So for me personally, I'll miss that in the future," he said. An AI game box? Part of what many people enjoy about physical games is collecting the boxes they come in and presenting them on their shelves. Willits said he thinks someone in the future might create some kind of "AI box" into which players can "upload all your games." "So maybe someone will do that," he said. Rising console prices Another major storyline in gaming in 2026 has been how video game consoles today are more expensive than ever. There are numerous reasons for this, including US President Donald Trump's tariffs, the AI-fueled impact on component and memory prices, and more. Sony and Microsoft raised prices on PlayStation and Xbox consoles so much that the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S consoles are now $150+ more expensive than they were when they launched in 2020. Nintendo, meanwhile, is hiking the price of the…

title: No, That Video Is Not An Accurate Representation Of Fable’s Combat
description: During Gamescom week, the Playground Games team working on Fable released a video showing off the game's combat. That video received a fair amount of backlash online, due to a boss appearing not to react to incoming attacks at all. Having played Fable myself now, and taking part in plenty of fights against both normal mob enemies and a boss, I think it's safe to say that the published video doesn't reflect my experience of Fable's combat. During my time with Fable at Gamescom, I played with two different builds crafted by the development team. In both, my primary weapon was a hammer, but I had access to a normal bow with the first build and a repeater crossbow with the second. Alongside these different weapons, I had entirely different spells available. The first loadout focused on all-out damage, with fire and lightning attacks available. The second loadout was more focused on crowd control, with an upgraded spell giving me the ability to raise groups of skeletal enemies into the air before bringing them crashing down to earth with a devastating thud. While I found the hammer pretty cumbersome, and it certainly wouldn't be my weapon of choice in a usual playthrough, the variety of spells meant I was only using my hammer to finish enemies off, or occasionally charging up my heavy attack to send them soaring off a cliff edge. Every enemy I encountered reacted to my incoming blows, and dodging, parrying, and deflecting attacks felt responsive, well-timed, and satisfying. I encountered at least six different types of enemy in my short hands-on time with the game. There was a wisp--a ghostly skeleton that, if not dispatched quickly, would bury itself beneath the ground to raise undead skeletons. Of those skeletons, there were armored variants, long-range sniper versions, and regular bony boys. Later on I came across a boss with an eerie green lantern for a skull, and while the combat became more difficult as hordes of mobs spawned around him, I never felt like my…

title: Gears Of War: E-Day Has A Battle Royale-Inspired PvP Mode Where You Can Strip The Flesh Off Enemies
description: Gears of War games have had some of the best multiplayer action around ever since the days of the first game, and for Gears of War: E-Day, developers at The Coalition are looking to give fans plenty of options for online fun. While the game's new take on Horde mode is shaping up to be the ultimate battlefield for players to enter, fans of traditional deathmatches aren't being left out in the cold either. At Gamescom, The Coalition spoke to GameSpot about E-Day's new Crucible mode and how it uses some battle royale inspiration to create a fast-paced round of 4v4 action. The PvP mode blends your typical Gears of War spatial control with battle royale mechanics, as teams must grab the Power Core, bring it to a designated active zone, and hold their position while the opposition closes in on them. The catch is that the Power Core restricts your mobility and limits which weapons you can use, meaning that your team will need to watch your back. The core stores a close-range electrical charge attack, and the carrier can unleash a charged blast at point-blank range to fry an enemy player, but this attack does have a long recharge time. Once the Power Core enters the scoring zone, it will begin to shrink. This, in turn, creates high-stakes zone pressure, forcing players into brutal standoffs as the space around them tightens. "It's very obviously inspired by battle royale games, but it's on a Gear-sized PVP map," creative director Matt Searcy said to GameSpot. "At the beginning of the map, there's lots of mobility, teams are moving around, you're trading the Power Core back and forth. But as the map goes on, you see defensive teams start to build up a front around the player they're protecting. And then, in awesome Gears fashion, the thing you're going to hold puts you at a slight disadvantage. So we gave you a heavy weapon that's basically a giant battery pack, and if somebody gets close to you within a really tight range, you can strip all the flesh off their body with a…

title: Saber Responds To AI Criticisms In Rideshare Game And Promises, “We Will Never Fire Someone And Replace Them With AI”
description: One of the biggest talking points in gaming today is the use of artificial intelligence, including generative AI. It's a hot-button issue, and few companies have faced the level of criticism about it as Saber has. The developer recently found itself in hot water after CEO Matthew Karch lashed out at Rideshare Stimulator's former writer who said they were laid off and replaced by ChatGPT. Now, Saber's chief creative officer, Tim Willits, has addressed the situation as well, promising that, "We will never fire someone and replace them with AI." For anyone just catching up, Rideshare Stimulator is an upcoming Saber game where players take on the role of an Uber- or Lyft-like driver and interact with them as they take them to their location. The developers freely admit to using generative AI in various capacities, and now Willits has shed more light on the situation. He said the game's main campaign features dialogue written by humans, but there is also a "free ride" mode where Rideshare Stimulator wants to be able to reference current events in the real world. "We use AI to generate that because we want to do it so fast," Willits said, adding that the plan is for weekly or biweekly updates with this kind of AI-generated content. Willits also clarified that some of Saber's other games, including the new Hellraiser, Turok, Stuntman, and Space Marine games, also do not use AI. Saber, like many other game companies, is experimenting with AI in various ways. "We want to figure this new technology out, and we don't know exactly where it's gonna go, and our players don't know where it's gonna go, so we're all... all of us are trying as a society to figure this out together," he said. "We want to experiment with it. I personally believe somebody [at] some game company will come up with such a brilliant idea, and we'll all be like, 'That's it.' We just need to get there." When asked specifically about claims that Saber is firing people and replacing them with AI, Willits said…

title: Hellraiser: Revival Is More Than Just Cenobites and Gore – 10 Things We Learned From Saber Interactive
description: October wouldn't feel right without a spooky game or two, and Hellraiser: Revival is shaping up to be a terrifying-- and horny --dive into the nightmarish fiction of author Clive Barker. So far, the game is looking like the kind of Hellraiser experience that defined the franchise throughout the '80s and early '90s, and at Gamescom, Saber Interactive sat down with GameSpot to talk about the game, how far they're willing to go to nail the vibe of Hellraiser, and more. Hellraiser: Revival launches for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S on October 8. Cliver Barker was a "permissive" partner The legendary creator of Hellraiser needed some convincing before he started collaborating with Saber Interactive, but once he was assured that the developers had a grasp of the Hellraiser franchise, he gave the studio the freedom to tell their own tale within that dark universe. "Clive Barker was such a permissive partner to work with," narrative director Anthony De Fault said. "He was really supportive of our ideas. He basically just wanted to make sure we understood Hellraiser as a franchise, and then, once he knew that we had the, we were channeling the same spirit that he was channeling back in the '80s, he just let us go." Capturing the soul of Hellraiser's greatest hits For the game, Saber Interactive aimed to capture the "soul" of the franchise, drawing not only from the recognizable visual elements established in the Hellraiser movies, but also from Clive Barker's original novella, The Hellbound Heart, which served as the source material for the franchise. "This game is a response, specifically to The Hellbound Heart, the first film, and Hellbound: Hellraiser 2, the second film," de Fault said. "So it's just the things that Clive was involved with that resonated really strongly with people back then. We wanted to make something that renewed that and had the same soul, but for a new medium and 40 years later." Barker was also credited as an executive producer on the third and…

title: Solve a mountain mystery via the medium of creepy cards in Hillthorn, which has an excellent demo

That game is Hillthorn, a spooky investigative cardgame from Fool Moon and Finnegan Motors - the latter also known for beaming corpo thriller Inhuman Resources: A Literary Machination. Hillthorn is the story of a detective hired to investigate a disappearance at a secluded mountain community. One of the first things you do, after hassling a worryingly stained forest ranger for directions, is cross a line of salt on the trail. Seems like something a person familiar with the occult would avoid doing, but you are a Private Eye, armed with logic and cynicism. Besides, all of this is presented via the medium of cards.
